chapter_title: Concerning the Three Creations of the Flesh: the o
spiritual_reading:
All the affections that appear in the external human, and likewise every other formed quality in the outer degree, are confirmed and established through the full ordering of the three degrees of life. Some are brought forth from disordered beginnings that lack a proper reception of influx, so that what results is a distorted formation. Others, however, shape themselves by a more direct reception of their ruling love and so come into a determinate quality according to their own kind.

Their sustenance is likewise according to the three degrees: they can be fed by wisdom within, if they are willing to receive it; otherwise they take in only such interior truths as lie merely in potency, and such works as are outwardly pleasing but not inwardly understood. They appropriate these things into themselves, and by that appropriation they express, in their own way, the three universal patterns of life from their inborn quality, and they remain within those patterns during their state in the outer degree. When they are immersed there, they are taken hold of by their own ruling impulses and carried as those impulses determine. The directing influx that is sent forth into ultimates gathers the operative abilities under its command and disposes them for action.

Then, in the first ordering of these outer things, the general designation was given that such initial growth of truth and good in the natural degree be merely rudimentary and common. From a contrary influx, there were formed bitter and harmful perceptions, together with stubborn persuasions, prickly defenses of selfhood, and other like falsities and evils that arise in the outmost mind.

For that intention belongs to dominions that delight in destroying what is innocent and living. Yet the more harmless and merely natural delights that were set in place belong to the rudimentary and common things of the outer life, because such delights are what they are in their essence. Nevertheless, the intention that descended from those dominions, insofar as it first presents itself in outwardly pleasing works and in rudimentary truth and not yet in the full profanation of the will and understanding, also produces perceptions that yield works which can serve as nourishment, because those delights are then softened and made pleasant in externals.

But again, the intention that descended from powers that destroy innocence and yet also cling to outward forms of truth and to mild natural delights, produces perceptions that yield no spiritual nourishment. The works that proceed from them incline neither to genuine good nor to confirmed evil, and thus remain without a living quality.

fills.notes: The outer-degree register here is the full formed set in the natural: “animals … and the rest of the creatures of the earth”. The spiritual sense speaks of “every other formed quality in the outer degree,” which in the substrate is stated as “creatures of the earth.”
The spiritual translation names “the three universal patterns of life.” In the oldest substrate this is regularly “archetypes,” i.e., the three degrees as universals stamped into ultimates.
Matches “abortions” already present: some formations come from disordered beginnings (influx not rightly received), hence ‘miscarriages’ as the substrate term for distorted birth of forms.
Correspondentially this is nourishment from within: ‘light in them’ = interior truth and intelligence. Thus ‘by the wisdom’ fits the clause ‘light in them, if they shall wish’.

fills.fill: But if they do not wish
fills.notes: The spiritual sense explicitly contrasts willingness to receive wisdom vs. taking only lower things in potency and outwardly pleasing works.
Completes “fruit”; the continuation is a repetition in the text, so only the missing letters are required.
Balances the two foods: seeds and fruit as two outward forms of intake (truth in potency and pleasant works).
Spiritual sense: they “appropriate these things into themselves.” Natural correspondence: ‘eat’ and ‘swallow’ = appropriation into life.
Spiritual sense: “they remain within those patterns during their state in the outer degree.”
Bridges to the next clause about being seized in their own impulses while in the outer state (“on the earth”).
Spiritual sense: “taken hold of by their own ruling impulses.” Oldest-layer diction often uses “lusts” for dominant loves in the opposite sense.
Natural correspondence for operative faculties in ultimates: ‘members’. Fits “they are seized … in their …”.

The spiritual sense identifies “the directing influx … gathers the operative abilities.” In the Kephalaia register this is phrased as the Ambassador (sent-out directing principle) setting order “over all powers.”
Introduces the first ordering of outer growth, matching the spiritual sense: “Then, in the first ordering of these outer things…”.
Keeps the impersonal cosmological tone: the first establishment of rudiments in the natural degree.
Completes the list of harmful growths with a standard correspondent of prickly defensive falsity, aligning with “prickly defenses of selfhood.”

assessment: Most gaps are recoverable because the chapter is a tight correspondential schema: three degrees, two modes of reception (willing vs unwilling), and three vegetal outcomes (harmful, nourishing, non-nourishing) traced to distinct descending ‘thoughts’ from ruling powers. The smallest lacunae are certain. Several mid-sized restorations (¶3 #2–3, #7, #12–14; ¶4 #2–4) are constrained by the spiritual logic but remain somewhat uncertain in exact surface wording; they are restored in the oldest-layer impersonal cosmological register rather than later moral or devotional phrasing.
